title: Local irreducibility and the neutral irreducible component of a group scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $G$ be a group scheme over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme], with identity point $e$. For every point $g\in G$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{G,g}$ has a unique minimal prime ideal, meaning a unique prime ideal minimal under inclusion among all prime ideals of that local ring. There is exactly one irreducible component $Z$ of $|G|$ containing $e$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]. With its reduced induced closed subscheme structure (the unique reduced closed subscheme with underlying subset $Z$), $Z$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. No finite-type or reducedness assumption on $G$ is imposed.

proof.text: First suppose $k$ is algebraically closed. Any irreducible reduced closed subscheme $T$ of $G$ is geometrically irreducible: apply [lem-sbc-subset-geometric-irreducibility] with $X=T$, $A=|T|$ and the identity extension $\Omega=k$. Its hypothesis is exactly irreducibility of $T$; algebraic closedness implies separable closedness since every polynomial splits. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] we may give every irreducible component its reduced closed structure. Every point, in particular $e$, lies in a component by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover].

source.place: Tag 047M (lemma-group-scheme-field-geometrically-irreducible), proof, second paragraph, preparation for the product argument

proof.text: Let $Z_1,Z_2$ be components containing $e$. By step 1 and [lem-sc-irreducible-product-over-field], $Z_1\times_k Z_2$ is irreducible. Its image under the restriction of multiplication is irreducible by [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-continuous-image] and lies in some component $W$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. It contains both $Z_i$: for $z\in Z_1$, the pair $(z,e)$ is a point of the product mapping to $z$, and likewise $(e,z)$ for $z\in Z_2$. These pairs exist as morphisms on $Z_i$ because the rational point $e$ factors through the reduced component: every function in its radical defining ideal vanishes in $\kappa(e)=k$, so its pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is zero. The unit identities of [def-sc-group-scheme] say that the composites with multiplication are the inclusions. Thus $Z_1,Z_2\subseteq W$, and maximality of components forces $Z_1=W=Z_2$.

source.place: Tag 047M (lemma-group-scheme-field-geometrically-irreducible), proof, second paragraph, multiplication and maximality

proof.text: For arbitrary $k$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Base change the group diagrams to give $G_\Omega$ its group structure; the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] preserves every equation. Steps 1--2 give a unique component $C$ of $G_\Omega$ through $e_\Omega$. Write $p:G_\Omega\to G$. The fibre $p^{-1}(e)$ has exactly one point, $e_\Omega$. Indeed the rational section $e$ gives field maps $k\to\kappa(e)\to k$ with composite the identity, by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field]. The second map is injective and contains all of $k$ in its image, so both maps are inverse isomorphisms. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and the fibre-product universal property, the fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(e)\otimes_k\Omega)=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, a one-point space [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tag 047M (lemma-group-scheme-field-geometrically-irreducible), proof, second paragraph, details of descent at the rational identity

proof.text: Let $Z$ be any component of $G$ containing $e$, which exists by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. By [lem-sfb-field-extension-irreducible-components], $p^{-1}(Z)$ is a nonempty union of components $D$ of $G_\Omega$. For each such $D$, its image $p(D)$ is a component contained in $Z$, hence equals $Z$ by maximality. Thus $D$ meets $p^{-1}(e)=\{e_\Omega\}$ and contains $e_\Omega$. Step 2 forces $D=C$. Consequently $p^{-1}(Z)=C$ and $p(C)=Z$. These equalities for every component through $e$ give uniqueness of $Z$. Apply [lem-sbc-subset-geometric-irreducibility] with $X=G$, $A=Z$, and $\Omega/k$: the inverse image is the nonempty irreducible subset $C$. It follows that $Z$ has irreducible nonempty inverse image under every field extension $E/k$. The reduced closed subscheme on $Z$ exists by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; its base change is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], whose support is this inverse image by [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and the fibre-product universal property. Thus this reduced component scheme is geometrically irreducible.

source.place: Tag 047M (lemma-group-scheme-field-geometrically-irreducible), proof, second paragraph, descent of assertions (2) and (3)

proof.text: For any scheme $X$ and $x\in X$, components containing $x$ correspond to minimal primes of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. To verify this without Noetherian hypotheses, choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $x$. Intersection with $U$ and closure in $X$ give mutually inverse correspondences between components of $X$ meeting $U$ and components of $U$: a nonempty open subset of an irreducible set is dense, so maximality in either space gives the inverse identities. Restrict to components containing $x$. They correspond by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] to minimal primes of $R$ contained in $\mathfrak p_x$. The inclusion-preserving prime bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization] identifies these with the minimal primes of $R_{\mathfrak p_x}$: every prime smaller than a prime below $\mathfrak p_x$ is still below $\mathfrak p_x$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $R_{\mathfrak p_x}$ with $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Applying this with $X=G$ and $x=e$ proves the unique-minimal-prime assertion at $e$.

source.place: Tag 047M (lemma-group-scheme-field-geometrically-irreducible), proof, first paragraph, components and minimal primes

proof.text: Fix $g\in G$ and put $K=\kappa(g)$. The canonical point $\operatorname{Spec}K\to G$ of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] and the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ give a $K$-rational point $g'$ of $G_K$ over $g$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The structure map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat by [lem-pc-field-extension-flat], so $G_K\to G$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. By [def-weil-flat-morphism] the induced local ring map $A=\mathcal O_{G,g}\to B=\mathcal O_{G_K,g'}$ is flat and local. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] it is faithfully flat and surjective on spectra. Translation by $g'$ is an isomorphism taking the identity to $g'$ [lem-sc-translation-automorphism], hence identifies $B$ with the local ring at the identity of $G_K$. Steps 3--5, applied over $K$, show that $B$ has a unique minimal prime $Q$.

source.place: Tag 047M (lemma-group-scheme-field-geometrically-irreducible), proof, first paragraph, rational lift, translation, and flat local map

proof.text: Every minimal prime $P$ of $A$ lifts to a prime $Q'$ of $B$ by the surjectivity in step 6. Choose a minimal prime $Q_0\subseteq Q'$ using [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] with ideal zero. Then $Q_0=Q$, and its contraction is a prime contained in $P$, hence equals $P$ by minimality. Thus every minimal prime of $A$ equals the contraction of $Q$. Such a prime exists: $A$ is a nonzero local ring, so its maximal ideal is prime, and [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] supplies a minimal prime beneath it. This proves assertion (1) for every $g$, completing the proof. Neither the component argument nor the local-ring argument imposed finite type or reducedness on $G$.
